evidence.title: Research synthesis for sparse-traffic marketplace measurement
evidence.excerpt: Observed fact: Shopify provides two relevant native signals for Shop marketplace visibility: Shop product impressions and sessions referred by UTM source `shop_app`, with selectable windows including today, last 7 days, and last 30 days. Observed fact: Shopify warns acquisition/session counts can vary because of analytics conditions like cookie consent and bot filtering. External research: Experiment duration should be set from traffic rate, baseline rate, and chosen minimum detectable effect (MDE); low-traffic contexts often require alternate tactics or more upstream proxy metrics. Interpretation: For a sparse-traffic manual marketplace test, the practical primary metric should be Shop product impressions or shop_app-referred sessions before downstream conversions, because these accumulate faster. Interpretation: A defensible minimum observation window is at least 30 days when traffic is sparse, since Shopify exposes a native 30-day view and broader experimentation guidance says runtime expands materially with low traffic and small effects. Interpretation: A practical decision threshold can be framed as 'do not judge until enough exposures accrue to detect a meaningful effect'; operationally, require either a full 30-day window or enough impressions/sessions to support an MDE-based comparison, and if that volume is not reached, treat results as inconclusive rather than negative. Hypothesis: For this team, a usable manual rule is to set a minimum effect threshold such as a large directional lift in impressions or shop_app sessions, because smaller effects are unlikely to be measurable with sparse marketplace traffic.

limitations: No Etsy-specific official analytics citation was available in the provided evidence; the closest official platform evidence is Shopify Shop analytics, so transfer to the target marketplace context is an interpretation rather than an observed Etsy fact.

The citations support using MDE/power-analysis concepts, but they do not provide a universal numeric threshold for sparse-traffic marketplace tests; any exact cutoff would be an assumption without local baseline data.
One cited low-traffic practitioner source was anecdotal Reddit discussion and was not relied on for the main recommendation.
Without the team's actual baseline impressions, referred sessions, click rate, or conversion rate, required sample size and exact decision thresholds cannot be calculated.

qualificationRequirements: Manual-only exploratory test: a human manually updates one listing message cluster at the top of the Shopify App Store listing; app behavior must remain unchanged.

Change one interpretable variable only: revise the top listing copy to make audience + catalog-audit job-to-be-done + read-only safety more explicit; keep pricing, category, support/privacy links, app behavior, and gallery assets constant during the first test window.
If the listing UI requires multiple coordinated top text fields, treat those edits as one message-cluster change and do not change screenshots, setup documentation, or category in the same window.
Record the exact before and after copy, the manual publish timestamp, and the start and end dates of the post-change observation window.

Minimum post-change observation rule: observe for at least 30 days after publish, or longer if traffic remains too sparse to accumulate any interpretable signal. This 30-day minimum is supported by external research synthesis noting Shopify exposes native 30-day analytics views and low-traffic experiments often need longer runtime.
Do not end the test early solely because the first days remain at zero; sparse traffic makes early stopping uninformative.
Interpret results directionally only; do not treat movement as causal proof because evidence quality is low and no impression-normalized baseline is available.
Human approval and manual marketplace edit are required before launch.

m6.expectedSupportingSignal: After the manual top-copy revision, scan_started_count rises from 0 to a higher observed count during the post-change window, ideally with app_opened_count also increasing and no deterioration in error_rate. A weaker but still supportive signal is that app_opened_count or request_count increases and at least one scan start occurs, which would directionally fit the message-clarity hypothesis.
m6.expectedWeakeningSignal: The hypothesis is weakened if, after the full minimum observation window, app_opened_count and scan_started_count both remain at 0, or if app_opened_count rises without any scan_started_count, or if error_rate worsens enough to make engagement changes uninterpretable. That would make the specific top-message explanation less convincing and leave low traffic or downstream friction as stronger alternatives.
m6.inconclusiveCondition: Results are inconclusive if the 30-day minimum window is not completed, if traffic remains too sparse for any meaningful before/after comparison, if other listing elements or external promotion changed during the same window, if tracking quality differs before versus after, or if no upstream exposure metric can be restored to contextualize observed counts.
contextToMonitor: Whether the live listing still has 0 reviews during the test window, because trust friction may suppress response independent of copy changes.
Whether the revised top copy makes read-only safety clearer without adding unsupported capability claims.
Whether the public listing materially changed after the 2026-08-25 manual capture before the test begins.
